title: JV eyes restoration of P130 billion for 2027 infra projects
summary: Senate finance committee chairman JV Ejercito is pushing for the restoration of some P130 billion in the proposed 2027 budget to fund railway, bridge and highway projects.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Senate finance committee chairman JV Ejercito is pushing for the restoration of some P130 billion in the proposed 2027 budget to fund railway, bridge and highway projects.

“The P130 billion cannot be compromised. It cannot be compromised as far as the Senate is concerned,” Ejercito said in an interview over dzBB yesterday. He added multipurpose building projects should be given smaller allocations.
Ejercito said the government must prioritize long-term infrastructure investments to help the Philippines attract more foreign investments and catch up with its Southeast Asian neighbors.

He said the P130 billion that he was pushing to restore should cover foreign-assisted projects, including the North-South Commuter Railway, Metro Manila Subway, Bataan-Cavite Interlink Bridge and Laguna Lakeshore Highway.

Ejercito acknowledged that reducing allocations for district projects could upset congressmen. But he said the government must strike a balance between addressing local needs and attracting investment that would generate jobs and boost economic growth.

He defended his decision to realign nearly P20 billion from the Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations or AICS and the Department of Health’s Medical Assistance Program to Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth).

He said the move would increase the state health insurer’s subsidy from P74 billion to P94.2 billion – from the P100 billion target – so it can expand its coverage and improve benefits under the Universal Health Care Law. He said the subsidy is short of the target due to what he called limited fiscal space.
Health Secretary Edwin Mercado noted a decline in the number of direct PhilHealth members regularly paying contributions, a situation that may require granting them incentives.

“What happened was because of what we call ‘immediate eligibility,’ there has been a drop in the number of paying members even though they have the capability to pay. That is why we thought of giving incentive if you are a regularly paying direct member,” Mercado said.
The DOH chief said their data showed that only one-third of members who have the capability to pay are paying contribution.

He said this was the reason for the recent launch of PhilHealth TAPAT, which aims to provide eligible direct contributors with additional 20 percent incentive in inpatient case rate starting January 2027.

During budget deliberations on Wednesday, P75 million was approved for the establishment by the Department of Labor and Employment of a Labor Attorneys’ Office that will provide free legal assistance to workers. The Senate approved DOLE’s P54.52-billion budget for 2027 during plenary session.

In another development, the Second Congressional Commission on Education reported yesterday that the 2027 budget program provides no funding for 29,588 new scholarship slots under the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority, potentially leaving thousands of learners from the poorest families without scholarship next year. — Christine Boton, Rhodina Villanueva, Bella Cariaso
